descriptionChirho: The proper noun Shishak (Hebrew שִׁישַׁק), referring to the Egyptian pharaoh (identified with Shoshenq I) who invaded Judah during the reign of Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:25; 2 Chronicles 12). All 8 occurrences refer to the same historical person. The single ketiv-variant occurrence (S140079) is an orthographic variant of the same name, not a distinct referent. Multilingual evidence is uniform: eng 'Shishak / [ketiv],' spa 'Sisac / [Shushaq],' hin शीशक, arb شيشق, kor 시샥 / 시삭, swa Shishaki. The minor spelling variations across translations confirm a single person.
